questions.stem: Given the stimulus, which topic sentence best opens the paragraph?

options.text: This paragraph discusses several bus data points.
options.misconception: announces topic instead of stating claim

options.text: Route 2 ridership fell on March weekdays.
Drivers face scheduling problems each month.
options.misconception: shifts focus to drivers not data

options.text: The council met to discuss transit budgets.

questions.explanation: A topic sentence states the data claim directly; vague openings fail.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Choose a contrast transition from a stimulus

stimulus.body: Stimulus K: March ridership comparison: Route 2 drops to 9,100 while Route 1 holds at 10,000.

questions.stem: Given the stimulus, which transition shows contrast?

options.text: In addition, Route 1 stayed stable.
For example, Route 1 stayed flat too.
By contrast, Route 1 ridership stayed flat.
Therefore, Route 1 must also decline.

questions.explanation: 'By contrast' names the opposing relation between falling and flat ridership.
questions.hint: Name the relation, not the fact.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Paraphrase a stimulus table value

stimulus.body: Stimulus L: Route 2 March ridership of 9,100, down from 12,400 in February.

questions.stem: Given the stimulus, which labelled paraphrase states Route 2's value?

options.text: Route 2 had 9,100 riders, which is bad.
The table says 9,100 for Route 2 in March.
options.misconception: quotes the table instead of paraphrasing

options.text: Route 2 ridership fell to 9,100 in March.
Route 2 March ridership: 9,100 (down from 12,400).

questions.explanation: A labelled paraphrase names quantity and context; quoting or omitting labels fails.

questions.learningObjective: Combine audience and thesis in two stages
questions.stem: First identify the audience, then choose the best thesis for the table.

options.text: Council members reviewing transit funding; Route 2 needs added weekday service.
Riders checking arrival times; all routes need more buses.
Drivers checking rosters; ridership never changes on Route 1.
Reporters seeking headlines; drivers need longer shifts.

questions.explanation: First the audience is council; then the thesis targets only documented Route 2 decline.

questions.learningObjective: Combine purpose and narrowing in two stages
questions.stem: First state the purpose, then narrow the claim for the table.

options.text: To entertain readers; all buses are always late.
To justify added service; Route 2 was late on three March weekdays.
To list arrival times; Route 1 stayed stable.
To compare shifts; drivers need longer breaks.

questions.explanation: Purpose is justification, and the claim must shrink to documented late days.
